entries.name: PEASS-ng
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Windows and Linux privilege-escalation suites (winPEAS, linPEAS): thousands of checks over services, paths, credentials and scheduled tasks. Used by pentesters sweeping for escalation paths; the de-facto standard priv-escalation audit on every engagement. (GPL-2.0-or-later)

entries.name: Evil-WinRM
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: The ultimate WinRM shell: PS history, tab completion, pass-the-hash logins, LAPS download and file exchange over WinRM/SMB. Used by pentesters who hold credentials and want the fastest route to an interactive shell; the WinRM shell every AD course teaches. (LGPL-3.0)

entries.name: Ligolo-ng
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Reverse socks5 tunneling for pivots: one TUN interface maps the agent's networks into your local routing table, no proxychains juggling. Used by red-teamers pivoting through internal ranges; the tunnel that made pivoting feel local. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Rubeus
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Kerberos interaction toolkit: AS-REP roasting, kerberoasting, pass-the-key, delegation abuse and diamond-ticket crafting. Used by AD attackers working the Kerberos layer; the GhostPack Kerberos swiss-army knife. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: CUPP
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Common User Passwords Profiler: generates targeted wordlists from a victim's biography — names, dates, hobbies, languages. Used by pentesters crafting personalized wordlists; the original target-specific wordlist generator. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: GoMapEnum
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: User enumeration and password spraying across SMB, Kerberos, NTLM and LDAP from a single Go binary. Used by red-teamers enumerating Windows users before a spray; the Go-native Windows enum-and-spray chain. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Legba
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Multiprotocol brute-forcer — SSH, FTP, SMTP, HTTP, MySQL, MSSQL, Redis and more — with one consistent CLI. Used by pentesters who want a single cracker for every protocol; evilsocket's answer to scattered brute-forcers. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: DonPAPI
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Remote DPAPI credential collection: Chrome cookies, Wi-Fi keys and custom DPAPI blobs gathered from many hosts without touching disk. Used by attackers chaining credentials across Windows estates; the remote DPAPI collector that opens every browser. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Certify
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Active Directory Certificate Services abuse toolkit: finds vulnerable certificate templates and chains ESC1-ESC8 from misconfigured CAs to domain compromise. Used by AD attackers auditing certificate services; the GhostPack tool that made AD CS a standard attack class. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: airgeddon
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: All-in-one wireless security suite: handshakes, evil-twin attacks, captive portals, WPS and pmkid workflows behind one interactive menu. Used by Wi-Fi auditors running the full wireless chain; the menu-driven Wi-Fi lab. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: SMBMap
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: SMB enumeration and share mapping: lists drives, permissions and writable shares, then downloads across a whole subnet. Used by pentesters enumerating Windows shares; the share-mapping staple since 2015. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Medusa
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Parallel login brute-forcer for many services with modular credential lists and host batching. Used by pentesters running credential attacks at scale; the speed-first login cracker of the THC-Hydra era. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Penelope
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Automated shell handler: catches reverse shells, upgrades them to fully interactive TTYs and logs every session. Used by pentesters tired of stty-raw gymnastics; the shell upgrader that saves the first ten minutes of every engagement. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Pacu
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: AWS exploitation framework: enumerates an account's services and chains misconfigurations into privilege-escalation paths. Used by cloud attackers chaining AWS misconfigs; the RhinoSecurity toolkit that defined open AWS offense. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: nomore403
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: 403/401 bypass toolkit: path-normalization tricks, header fuzzing and method overrides that turn forbidden pages into accessible ones. Used by bug hunters probing access-control edges; the 403-bypass playbook codified. (MIT)

entries.name: gotestwaf
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: WAF assessment harness: fires ~900 benign-and-attack test cases (OWASP, fauxpas, shadowd) at a protected path and grades what the WAF actually blocks, with a hardening report. Used by pentesters measuring WAF effectiveness before tuning payloads; the Wallarm WAF benchmark. (MIT)

entries.name: cvcemap
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: ProjectDiscovery's CVE-to-version mapping (repo: vulnx): fingerprint a component and get the live CVE list for the exact version in one command. Used by recon pipelines mapping component exposure; the projectdiscovery take on CVE mapping. (MIT)

entries.name: tlsx
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: TLS-focused recon: cipher and certificate enumeration, SAN extraction and TLS-version probing with the projectdiscovery CLI ergonomics. Used by recon pipelines snapshotting TLS posture; the fast TLS recon companion. (MIT)

entries.name: cdncheck
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Detects whether a host sits behind a CDN or known cloud provider before you scan it, from ProjectDiscovery's curated provider list. Used by recon pipelines avoiding wasted scans on protected edges; the suite's CDN gatekeeper. (MIT)

entries.name: findomain
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Subdomain discovery through certificate transparency and multiple data sources with a database backend. Used by bug hunters building subdomain inventories; one of the fastest passive enumerators of its generation. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: knockpy
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Subdomain enumeration by wordlist and CT logs with wildcard detection built in. Used by pentesters running dictionary subdomain passes; the classic knock turned into a maintained Python tool. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: subcat
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Subdomain discovery through search-engine and passive sources, built for pipeline use. Used by recon chains wanting passive subdomain sets; the lightweight passive-enum addition. (MIT)

entries.name: graphw00f
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: GraphQL fingerprinter: detects the engine behind an endpoint — Apollo, Hasura, Yoga and the rest — from behavioral signatures. Used by pentesters preparing engine-specific GraphQL payloads; the fingerprinter that tells you which GraphQL you are attacking. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: graphinder
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: GraphQL endpoint discovery: expands domains from CT logs and certificate SANs, then probes permutations with a wordlist to find unlisted GraphQL endpoints. Used by bug bounty hunters hunting hidden GraphQL surfaces; Escape Technologies' dockerized finder that pairs with graphw00f. (MIT)

entries.name: gowitness
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Website screenshot recon: headless Chrome captures whole asset inventories and serves them in a browsable report. Used by bug hunters eyeballing thousands of hosts at once; the recon screenshot standard. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: FAVIHUNTER
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Favicon-based asset hunting: mmh3 favicon hashes match your targets' properties against public scan datasets. Used by attack-surface mappers looking for forgotten properties; the favicon-hash bridge for asset discovery. (MIT)

entries.name: gitjacker
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Leaks .git directories from misconfigured webservers and reconstructs the repository history. Used by bug hunters checking for exposed source; the git-dump attack automated. (Unlicense)

entries.name: InfoHound
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: OSINT search-engine framework: crawls people, emails, domains and leaks into structured intelligence reports. Used by investigators building target dossiers; the i2CAT open intelligence engine. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: Investigo
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Username and email finder across social networks and forums with a clean CLI. Used by OSINT researchers tracing identities; a long-standing social presence mapper. (MIT)

entries.name: EmailHarvester
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Email enumeration via search engines and public sources. Used by OSINT collectors gathering corporate footprints; the maldevel classic that keeps earning its place. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Instaloader
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Instagram archiving: photos, stories, captions and metadata downloaded rate-limit-aware. Used by investigators archiving social evidence; the Instagram archiver that respects both public data and platform limits. (MIT)

entries.name: gallery-dl
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Command-line downloader for image galleries and video collections from hundreds of sites, for authorized archiving and OSINT work. Used by archivers preserving online media; the gallery downloader that covers almost every platform. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: TestDisk
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Partition-table and file recovery: undeletes, fixes boot sectors and rescues lost partitions across most filesystems. Used by DFIR and ops teams rescuing broken disks; the cgsecurity recovery classic. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: androguard
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Reverse-engineering framework for Android: DEX/ODEX parsing, decompilation, static analysis and APK diffing in Python. Used by mobile analysts tearing APKs apart; the Android RE foundation. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: hurl
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: HTTP requests in plain text: run and test endpoints with a human-readable format, assertions and CI-ready reports. Used by API testers scripting endpoint checks; the plain-text HTTP runner. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: chisel
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: TCP tunnel over HTTP: a single client/server binary pairs port-forwards through restrictive egress. Used by red-teamers tunneling through web-exit-only networks; the jpillora tunnel standard. (MIT)

entries.name: GoReplay
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Traffic replay: capture production HTTP and replay it at scale against staging — shadow testing with real load instead of synthetic. Used by testers replaying real traffic; the open-core replay standard. (LGPL-3.0, open-core)

entries.name: Slither
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Solidity static analysis: 90+ detectors for reentrancy, variable shadowing and dangerous patterns in smart contracts. Used by auditors reviewing Solidity; the smart-contract SAST standard. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: AFL++
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: The fuzzer: coverage-guided mutation with modern instrumentation for everything from parsers to kernels. Used by researchers finding memory corruption; the community fuzzer that keeps out-performing the original AFL. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: pip-audit
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Scans Python environments for known vulnerabilities against the PyPA advisory database. Used by Python shops securing their dependency trees; the official PyPA audit tool. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: xeol
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: End-of-life dependency detection: finds packages past their support lifetime in SBOMs and repositories. Used by DevSecOps teams tracking EOL software; the lifecycle-aware scanner. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: CodeQL
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Semantic code analysis from GitHub: query code as a database and hunt vulnerability classes across languages with variant analysis. Used by security researchers hunting bug classes at scale; free for open-source research. (MIT)

entries.name: cloudfox
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Cloud attack-surface auditor: maps IAM, services and privileges across AWS, Azure and GCP for engagement prep. Used by cloud pentesters building their attack map; the BishopFox cloud 'who am I' reconnaissance tool. (MIT)

entries.name: GCP Scanner
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Google Cloud security scanner: enumerates projects, services, IAM and exposure across a GCP organization. Used by cloud auditors assessing GCP estates; the official google/gcp_scanner. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Tracee
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Container runtime security tracing with eBPF: follows syscalls and events to detect suspicious behavior in real time. Used by runtime-security teams watching containers live; Aquasecurity's eBPF sensor. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Hayabusa
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Windows event-log analysis and threat hunting: parses EVTX at speed, detects with built-in Sigma rules and builds timelines. Used by DFIR hunters triaging Windows estates; the Yamato-Security log analyzer. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: Netlas
entries.section: Highlights
entries.description: Internet-registry search across ASNs, DNS, certificates and network data with a generous free tier for researchers. Used by OSINT and attack-surface work at zero budget; the registry search with the free-research tier. (free tier)

entries.name: Metasploit Framework
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The world's most-used pentest framework; thousands of validated modules for exploitation, post-engagement evidence gathering and reporting in authorized tests. Used by professional penetration testers and red teams in authorized engagements; the open-source counterpart to commercial exploitation platforms like Core Impact and Cobalt Strike.

entries.name: Nmap
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The original network mapper: port, service and OS discovery plus the NSE scripting engine for everything from TLS audits to SMB checks. Used by virtually every network security auditor on earth; the open standard that commercial scanners built their discovery phases on.

entries.name: Burp Suite Community Edition
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The industry-standard intercepting proxy for manual web testing; the free tier is where nearly every bug hunter starts. Used by web penetration testers as their daily intercepting proxy; the free tier of the industry-standard Burp Suite Professional. (free, proprietary)

entries.name: Nuclei
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Template-driven vulnerability scanner; the huge community template corpus gives it detection breadth no single scanner matches. Used by bug bounty hunters and enterprise security teams alike for template-driven scanning at scale; a free staple that rivals paid web-scanning engines for public attack-surface checks.

entries.name: afrog
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Fast cross-platform vulnerability scanner driven by a 1,700+ community-maintained YAML PoC corpus covering CVE, CNVD, unauthorized-access, default-password and fingerprinting checks. Used by bug bounty hunters and pentesters running corpus-driven scans; the open-source scanner with one of the largest community PoC collections. (MIT)

entries.name: OWASP ZAP
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The open-source intercepting proxy and scanner — a full free Burp alternative with CI/CD integration and a big add-on ecosystem. Used by web pentesters, QA teams and bug bounty beginners.

entries.name: OpenTRAP
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Free open-source Burp Suite alternative: an intercepting proxy with Repeater, Intruder, a Collaborator-style OAST server and the built-in OWASP ZAP scanner in one desktop suite. Used by web pentesters who want a full proxy workbench without a license; the open alternative built on the ZAP engine.. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: hetty
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: HTTP toolkit for security research: an intercepting proxy with scope rules, request composer and replay, and a GraphQL management API in one self-hosted Go binary. Used by security researchers and bug hunters who want a scriptable, self-hosted proxy workbench; the open-source HTTP research toolkit. (MIT)

entries.name: Akto
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Self-hosted API-security platform that builds a continuous API inventory from mirrored runtime traffic and runs business-logic tests (BOLA, BFLA, OWASP API Top 10) in CI. Used by API security teams testing business-logic flaws generic DAST misses; the open-source alternative to API-scanning SaaS. (MIT)

entries.name: sqlmap
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The definitive SQL injection detection and exploitation tool for authorized web application testing. Used by penetration testers everywhere for SQL injection proof; the definitive free SQLi automation tool with no real commercial equal. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: unKover
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The 403 access-bypass tester: a 13-technique battery (path rewrites, header tricks, HTTP method and version shifts) that turns forbidden endpoints into authorized access. Used by web pentesters proving 403s are misconfigurations during engagements; the focused free alternative to commercial authz-testing modules. (MIT per README)

entries.name: jwt-hack
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: JWT attack toolkit: cracking, payload generation, alg-confusion and claim-abuse checks for JSON Web Tokens in one CLI. Used by bug bounty hunters and pentesters auditing token-based authentication; the dedicated free toolkit for the JWT bug class.. (MIT)

entries.name: Impacket
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The standard Python library for low-level Windows protocol work (SMB, LDAP, Kerberos); powers wmiexec/secretsdump-class tooling and AD assessments. Used by red teamers and AD security researchers; the Python underpinning of countless offensive and defensive toolkits.

entries.name: MITRE Caldera
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Scalable adversary-emulation platform built on ATT&CK; run purple-team exercises that prove your detections actually fire. Used by red teams and purple teams for automated adversary emulation; the open-source alternative to commercial breach-attack-simulation platforms like AttackIQ and SafeBreach.

entries.name: Realm
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Open-source adversary-emulation framework with cross-platform implants and Terraform-driven C2 infrastructure for authorized red teams. Used by red teams running repeatable, scoped adversary emulation; the open-source alternative to commercial adversary-simulation platforms. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: BloodHound
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Maps the shortest attack paths through Active Directory; defenders run it to find and fix their way to Domain Admin. Used by Active Directory pentesters to map hidden attack paths; the standard tool defenders also run to harden AD.

entries.name: MobSF
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: All-in-one mobile app security: static + dynamic analysis for Android/iOS in a single pipeline. Used by mobile app security testers for static and dynamic analysis; the open-source alternative to commercial mobile app testing suites. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: WPScan
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Black-box WordPress scanner: plugin/theme enumeration and version-based vuln lookups. Used by WordPress security auditors and managed-service providers; the standard black-box WordPress scanner, free alternative to paid WP security suites. (free for non-commercial use)

entries.name: Bettercap
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The Swiss-army knife for authorized network assessments: ARP/DNS spoofing, MITM proxies, WiFi and BLE modules. Used by network penetration testers for authorized MITM analysis; the modern successor to Ettercap in most toolkits. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Nikto
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Venerable web-server scanner; noisy but thorough on server misconfigurations and default files. Used by web server auditors for two decades; the venerable free complement to commercial web scanners' misconfiguration checks. (GPL-3.0; DB files have custom terms)

entries.name: h5i
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Agent-native web-security workspace: deterministic recon, secrets scanning, DOM post-message auditing and CI regression checks — fully usable without any LLM key. Used by security engineers wanting agent-native, deterministic web checks; a newer open alternative to dashboard-driven commercial scanners. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: goshs
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Hardened HTTP file-transfer server built for engagements: upload/download, authentication, access control and TLS — the modern replacement for `python -m http.server`. Used by pentesters on engagements as a hardened file-transfer server; the security-hardened alternative to spinning up ad-hoc Python servers.

entries.name: Dalfox
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Fast XSS scanner with DOM-aware analysis and a strong payload set; the modern XSS go-to. Used by bug bounty hunters for fast, DOM-aware XSS scanning; a favorite free alternative to Burp's scanner for XSS-only sweeps.

entries.name: pphack
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Advanced client-side prototype-pollution scanner for JavaScript-heavy web apps. Used by bug bounty hunters auditing front-end pollution sinks; the dedicated free scanner for this bug class. (MIT)

entries.name: NetExec
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: CrackMapExec's actively maintained successor; audit credential hygiene and service misconfigurations across whole subnets. Used by internal network auditors and AD pentesters for credential-hygiene sweeps.

entries.name: Responder
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: LLMNR/NBT-NS/MDNS poisoner; the fastest way to demonstrate credential-leak exposure on an authorized internal network. Used by internal penetration testers to demonstrate credential exposure on enterprise networks; the canonical LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoner. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: commix
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Automated OS command injection detection and exploitation for web tests. Used by web pentesters for command-injection proof; a focused free tool that complements general-purpose commercial scanners. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Ghauri
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: A strong sqlmap alternative for error/union/blind SQLi with clever parameter tampering; slower release cadence but unique value. Used by bug bounty hunters for tricky blind, error-based and time-based SQLi.

entries.name: NoSQLMap
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: NoSQL injection testing for MongoDB, CouchDB and Redis-backed apps: injection, enumeration and data extraction for document-store backends. Used by pentesters attacking NoSQL endpoints where SQLi tooling does not apply; the reference NoSQL injection toolkit since 2013. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: 2MNY Website Vulnerability Scanner
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Open-source web vulnerability scanner with 202 deterministic modules: OWASP Top 10, XSS/SQLi/SSRF, subdomain takeover, WordPress and AI/LLM surface checks, CVSS-scored evidence and HTML/PDF reports. Self-hosted via Docker. Used by security teams that want evidence-backed, deterministic scanning they can self-host; the open-source alternative to paid scanner SaaS for website attack surfaces. (maintainer's project)

entries.name: masscan
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: The fastest TCP port scanner on earth; scan the whole internet in minutes — on networks you're authorized to test. Used by researchers and recon teams for internet-scale port discovery. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: RustScan
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Modern Rust port scanner that finds open ports in seconds and pipes them straight into Nmap. Used by bug bounty hunters and sysadmins for fast port discovery with Nmap piping; a modern free alternative to legacy scanners. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: crossfyre-toolchain
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Recon-to-scan toolchain of five Rust engines — subdomain discovery, port scanning, content fuzzing, fingerprinting and vulnerability checks — plus a self-hosted OAST server that confirms each finding before it reports it. Used by bug bounty hunters running fast terminal-first pipelines; the Rust-native alternative to stitched-together shell toolkits.. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Tsunami
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Google's security scanner for large fleets, focused on reliably exploitable high-severity flaws with few false positives. Used by security teams scanning large fleets of internet-facing services; Google's open-source answer to commercial enterprise web scanners.

entries.name: VulnRadar
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Self-hostable web vulnerability scanner with 855+ deterministic checks, stable finding IDs for scan-to-scan diffing, severity-rated reports and actionable fix guidance. Used by teams wanting instant, shareable scan reports without a SaaS subscription; the self-hosted alternative to commercial web scanners.. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Prism X
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Automated enterprise network security risk detection: one command sweeps hosts and services for exploitable findings like the commercial AWVS/fscan class. Used by internal teams risk-scoring their own networks; the free enterprise-web risk scanner. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: WAVSS
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Audit-first web vulnerability scanner for common flaws like SQLi and XSS, with domain-ownership verification, DoS-avoidant pacing and PDF reports with remediation guidance. Used by auditors scanning client sites safely under strict rules of engagement; the audit-focused alternative to exploit-heavy scanners. (no license yet — verify before reuse)

entries.name: SoliTools
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: High-accuracy web security scanner in Go built on the rule that a finding must be worth a human's time — precision beats recall at every decision point. Used by bug bounty hunters who want quiet, high-precision scans; the precision-first free scanner.. (MIT)

entries.name: Hakscan
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Fast, self-contained vulnerability scanner shipped as a single Go binary — covers web apps, APKs and binaries, extensible with JSON and nuclei YAML templates. Used by bug bounty hunters wanting one-binary scanning across target types; the portable free scanner for quick triage.. (MIT)

entries.name: wafw00f
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Fingerprints the web application firewall sitting in front of a site so you know exactly what you're testing against. Used by pentesters planning engagements to fingerprint WAFs first; the standard free WAF detector.

entries.name: wapiti
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Open-source black-box web vulnerability scanner that crawls and audits without needing a browser. Used by web pentesters and CI pipelines for black-box web scanning; a solid free alternative to paid web vulnerability scanners. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: WhatWeb
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Identifies what a website is built with — frameworks, CMSs, servers and versions — in one command. Used by recon teams to fingerprint what a site runs on; the standard free tech-identifier behind many commercial recon feeds. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: GitTools
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Recovers an exposed `.git` directory into full source and commit history — audit your servers before attackers do. Used by bug bounty hunters to recover exposed .git directories into full source; the go-to free tool for this bug class.

entries.name: kiterunner
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: API route brute-forcer with method-aware wordlists derived from Swagger specs; dormant upstream, still the reference. Used by API security testers brute-forcing routes with method-aware wordlists; the open-source alternative to commercial API discovery scans. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: osmedeus
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Workflow engine that chains recon and scanning into scheduled, repeatable attack-surface pipelines. Used by recon teams automating full attack-surface workflows; the free alternative to commercial ASM platforms for scheduled recon.

entries.name: PWN
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Ruby offensive-security automation framework that orchestrates Burp, Nessus, OpenVAS, ZAP and other engines into scripted authorized engagements. Used by pentesters chaining commercial and open engines from one Ruby CLI; the glue layer for multi-engine engagements. (MIT)

entries.name: ettercap
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

entries.description: Weaponized web shell providing a stealthy backdoor and post-exploitation modules over HTTP. Used by pentesters and red teamers; a modular webshell framework. (GPL-3.0)

entries.description: Rogue access point framework for automated Wi-Fi phishing attacks, capturing credentials via fake captive portals. Used by red teamers; a well-known Wi-Fi phishing toolkit. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Wifite
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Automated wireless attack tool that streamlines Wi-Fi auditing workflows. Used by penetration testers; a popular free scripted wireless testing tool.

entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Automated wireless auditor that simplifies attacking WEP, WPA and WPS networks with minimal user interaction. Used by penetration testers and wireless auditors; a popular automation wrapper. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Windows Exploit Suggester
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Suggests exploits based on Windows OS versions and patch levels. Used by penetration testers and red teams; a practical offensive reconnaissance utility. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: XSRFProbe
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: CSRF audit and exploitation toolkit that scans applications for cross-site request forgery weaknesses. Used by web pentesters and bug-bounty hunters; a dedicated CSRF testing suite. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: xssor2
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: XSS exploitation toolkit that lets testers hack with JavaScript payloads in browser contexts. Used by web pentesters and bug-bounty hunters; a classic XSS research utility. (BSD-2-Clause)

entries.name: XSStrike
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Cross-site scripting detection and exploitation tool with advanced payload generation and fuzzing. Used by web pentesters; a capable XSS-focused scanner. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Zphisher
entries.section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
entries.description: Advanced phishing tool with tunneling support for exposing local phishing pages. Used by security researchers and penetration testers; a widely starred social-engineering framework. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: CrowdSec
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Collaborative behavior-detection engine with a global IP-reputation network; the modern Fail2ban, 60x faster and IPv6-ready. Used by server administrators and hosting providers; the open-source, crowdsourced alternative to commercial WAF and bot-management services.

entries.name: Fail2ban
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The classic log-watching IPS that bans brute-forcing IPs; still the default answer on every Linux server. Used by sysadmins on millions of servers to stop brute force; the classic free guard no commercial tool needed to replace. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Lynis
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Agentless system auditing and hardening with CIS/PCI-DSS-aligned findings; runs anywhere in minutes. Used by system auditors running CIS-style hardening checks; the open-source alternative to commercial compliance scanners for Linux/Unix hosts. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: OpenSnitch
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Interactive application firewall (Little Snitch for Linux): allow/deny every outbound connection per process. Used by Linux power users and admins wanting per-application firewall control; the open equivalent of Little Snitch on macOS. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: testssl.sh
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Command-line TLS/SSL configuration auditor: protocols, ciphers, chains, vulnerabilities, grading — no agent required. Used by TLS auditors and pentesters everywhere; the free command-line alternative to Qualys SSL Labs for server-side TLS grading. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: ComplianceAsCode content
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The open SCAP/Baseline rule corpus for RHEL, Ubuntu and friends; the content that powers OpenSCAP-style audits. Used by compliance and platform teams applying SCAP hardening profiles; the open-source ruleset commercial compliance products build on.

entries.name: ssh-audit
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: SSH server configuration auditor: algorithms, keys and best-practice flags in one run. Used by server hardening teams to audit SSH configurations and algorithms; the standard free SSH auditor. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: OSSEC
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The original open-source HIDS: log analysis, file integrity and rootkit detection (Wazuh's ancestor). Used by SOC teams on a budget for host intrusion detection; the veteran open HIDS that predates commercial EDR. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Coraza
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: ModSecurity-compatible WAF engine in Go; the actively developed successor for OWASP CRS deployments. Used by platform teams embedding a WAF engine inside Go services.

entries.name: OWASP Core Rule Set
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The world's most-deployed WAF ruleset; battle-tested protection for web servers, tuned for ModSecurity and Coraza. Used by WAF administrators on nginx, Apache and Coraza; the free ruleset protecting more sites than most commercial WAF feeds.

entries.name: dev-sec hardening collection
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Battle-tested Ansible roles for OS, SSH, nginx and MySQL baselines; hardening as code. Used by DevOps teams enforcing server baselines as code; the open-source alternative to commercial configuration-compliance agents.

entries.name: OPNsense
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Open-source firewall/router distro with IDS, VPN and reporting — a pfSense successor built on HardenedBSD. Used by network administrators as a full open-source firewall/router; the business-ready free alternative to commercial UTM appliances. (BSD-2)

entries.name: BunkerWeb
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Next-gen open WAF built on nginx: HTTPS, bot mitigation and network protections on by default. Used by web admins wanting a next-gen open-source WAF in front of their sites; the self-hosted alternative to Cloudflare's managed WAF. (AGPL-3.0)

entries.name: open-appsec
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: ML-driven prevention engine that stops OWASP Top 10 and zero-day web attacks without signatures. Used by security teams deploying machine-learning WAF protection; an open-source alternative to commercial ML-based WAF products.

entries.name: OpenRASP
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Runtime application self-protection: instrument the app itself so attacks get blocked from the inside. Used by AppSec teams adding runtime self-protection to apps; the open-source alternative to commercial RASP vendors.

entries.name: OpenVPN
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The industry-standard open-source VPN daemon for site-to-site and remote-access tunnels. Used by IT teams everywhere; the open-source alternative to commercial VPN gateways. (GPL-2.0 core, component exceptions)

entries.name: stunnel
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Universal TLS wrapper that adds encryption to any TCP service in minutes. Used by admins adding TLS to legacy services; the free universal TLS wrapper. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: OpenSSH
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The world's default secure remote-access suite: encrypted shells, tunnels and key management. Used on virtually every Linux server on earth; the open standard for secure remote access that commercial SSH servers complement, not replace. (BSD-style)

entries.name: ClamAV
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The open-source antivirus engine that powers mail gateways and file-screening pipelines everywhere. Used on countless mail gateways and Linux file screens; the AV engine many commercial mail filters embed. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: AIDE
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment: file-integrity monitoring that alerts the moment system files change. Used by hardening teams for file-integrity monitoring; the free open alternative to commercial FIM modules. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Tor
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The anonymity network: routed egress through thousands of volunteer relays; the standard for privacy-preserving research access. Used by privacy-focused researchers, journalists and investigators; the free anonymity network with no commercial equivalent. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: Netfilter/iptables
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The Linux kernel's native packet-filtering framework; the foundation every host firewall build starts from. Used by every Linux firewall admin; the kernel-level packet filter that commercial Linux firewalls wrap a UI around. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: SELinux
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Mandatory access control for Linux: policy-based confinement that survives a compromised application. Used by hardened enterprise Linux deployments; the mandatory access control standard in RHEL-family distributions. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: OpenBSD PF
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The packet filter famous for correctness and readable rules; the syntax OpenBSD, pfSense and OPNsense share. Used by OpenBSD and firewall admins; the famously audited packet filter behind many security appliances. (ISC)

entries.name: checksec.sh
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: One-shot binary hardening audit: NX, canaries, PIE, RELRO and fortify flags in a single run. Used by exploit developers and binary auditors checking hardening mitigations; the standard free one-liner for this job. (BSD-3-Clause)

entries.name: Vuls
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Agentless vulnerability scanner for servers and containers, with CVE reporting across Linux and FreeBSD fleets. Used by server admins for agentless vulnerability scanning; the open-source alternative to Nessus for host patch audits. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: SpamAssassin
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The veteran open-source spam filter; bayesian scoring and rule engine at the mail gateway. Used by mail administrators on countless gateways; the veteran open-source anti-spam engine many commercial filters license. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Fleet
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Osquery fleet management: device visibility and policy enforcement at scale, open core with a free tier. Used by IT and security teams managing osquery fleets at scale; the open-source alternative to commercial device management and EDR consoles. (MIT, open core)

entries.name: shellfirm
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: A pre-execution guard for your shell: challenges dangerous commands (rm -rf, kubectl delete) before they run. Used by engineers protecting themselves from dangerous commands; a lightweight open guardrail before your shell executes rm -rf. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Qubes OS
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: The security-by-compartmentalization desktop OS; " reasonably secure" by architecture, not by antivirus. Used by journalists, researchers and high-risk users; the compartmentalized security desktop with no commercial counterpart. (GPL-2.0)

entries.name: Neo23x0 auditd config
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Florian Roth's hardened auditd rule set: the Linux logging baseline used across incident-response teams. Used by blue teams hardening Linux audit collection; the widely-forked open auditd baseline behind many SOC deployments. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: unmask
entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Self-hosted privacy-first bot management gateway with verified-crawler bypass. Used by teams filtering bot traffic without third-party SaaS; the self-hosted bot-defense gateway. (Apache-2.0)

entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools
entries.description: Go implementation of the Cloud Security Alliance's Network-infrastructure Hiding Protocol: conceals ports, IPs and domains behind a cryptographically signed knock gate — services stay invisible until the client proves trust. Used by zero-trust teams making infrastructure undiscoverable to mass and AI-driven scanning; the reference open implementation of CSA NHP. (Apache-2.0)

entries.section: 🛡️ The Bastion — Hardening & Defensive Infrastructure Tools

entries.section: 🗺️ The Cartographers — Recon, OSINT & Attack-Surface Mapping Tools
entries.description: The HTTP prober: filter thousands of hosts by status, title, tech, CDN and TLS in a single pass. Used by bug bounty hunters triaging alive hosts from mass subdomain lists; the ProjectDiscovery prober in nearly every recon pipeline.

entries.section: 🗺️ The Cartographers — Recon, OSINT & Attack-Surface Mapping Tools

entries.section: 🗺️ The Cartographers — Recon, OSINT & Attack-Surface Mapping Tools

entries.name: Cutter

entries.description: Online cipher and code identification/decoding tool covering classical ciphers, modern cryptographic challenges, and CTF tasks. Used by CTF players and puzzle solvers; a broad reference for decoding. (free, proprietary)

entries.name: espi0n/Dockerfiles
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Dockerfiles packaging various OSINT tools for easy deployment. Used by OSINT practitioners; a convenient containerized toolset.

entries.name: Fluentd
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Log collector and forwarder gathering logs from many sources and routing them to other systems for processing. Used by platform engineers; a clean open-source log pipeline component. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Frida
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Dynamic instrumentation toolkit for hooking and inspecting running processes. Used by reverse engineers and mobile security researchers; a leading free instrumentation framework.

entries.name: Ghidra
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Open-source software reverse engineering framework for disassembly and decompilation. Used by reverse engineers and malware analysts; a leading free RE suite.

entries.name: GNU Radio
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Free and open-source signal processing framework providing blocks for modulation, demodulation, filtering, and spectrum analysis with graphical flowgraphs. Used by RF engineers and SDR developers; the foundational toolkit for software radio work. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Gpredict
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Real-time satellite tracking and orbit prediction software for identifying satellite passes over ground stations and accounting for Doppler shift. Used by satellite operators and SDR hobbyists; a reliable pass-planning tool. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: GQRX
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Software defined radio receiver built on GNU Radio and Qt supporting HackRF, RTL-SDR, Airspy, and USRP hardware for AM/FM/SSB reception. Used by RF hobbyists and security researchers; a popular general-purpose SDR frontend. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Inspectrum
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Offline spectrum analysis tool with spectrogram visualization, zoom and pan for examining captured RF signals including Iridium bursts. Used by RF analysts and satellite researchers; a focused tool for inspecting recorded IQ data. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: IPObfuscator
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Simple tool converting an IP address to its DWORD representation. Used by pentesters; a small obfuscation helper.

entries.name: LaTeX
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: High-quality typesetting system often used to produce professional security reports. Used by technical writers and pentesters; a standard for polished document output.

entries.name: LibreWolf
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Privacy-hardened Firefox fork with no telemetry, uBlock Origin pre-installed, DuckDuckGo default search, and built-in DNS-over-HTTPS. Used by privacy-conscious desktop users; a hardened daily browser. (MPL-2.0)

entries.name: LIEF
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Library for parsing and modifying executable formats. Used by reverse engineers and security tool developers; a free cross-platform binary analysis library.

entries.name: Lychee
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Fast broken link checker that can be used to spot dead or suspicious links across sites and repositories. Used by developers and security testers; a utility with light security-adjacent value. (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Markdown
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Lightweight markup language for clean, portable report writing. Used by security professionals and developers; a simple way to author readable documentation.

entries.name: MetaDefender

entries.description: Multi-engine file and URL malware scanning service. Used by analysts and defenders; a convenient reputation and malware check. (free tier)

entries.name: mosquitto_sub
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: MQTT client for subscribing to IoT device topics, used to test broker authentication and topic ACL enforcement. Used by IoT testers; a standard broker utility. (EPL-2.0)

entries.name: Mullvad Browser
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Collaboration between Tor Project and Mullvad providing Tor Browser's anti-fingerprinting protections without requiring the Tor network. Used by privacy advocates; a strong anti-fingerprinting browser. (free, proprietary)

entries.name: OllyDbg
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: 32-bit assembler-level debugger for Windows binaries. Used by reverse engineers and malware analysts; a classic free debugging tool. (free, proprietary)

entries.name: OnionShare
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Open-source tool for securely and anonymously sharing files, hosting websites, and chatting over the Tor network via temporary onion services. Used by privacy advocates; a simple Tor-based sharing tool. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: PEiD
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: Privacy Badger
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Automatic tracker blocker from the Electronic Frontier Foundation that learns which domains track you and blocks them without configuration. Used by privacy-conscious browsers; an EFF-backed defense. (GPL-3.0)

entries.name: Proton Mail

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: PyModbus
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
entries.description: Python Modbus library used for simulating industrial environments and crafting custom protocol packets for ICS security testing and fuzzing. Used by ICS developers and testers; a widely adopted building block for Modbus tooling.

entries.name: QEMU
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: ReClass.NET
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: RetDec
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: Rizin

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: SimpleLogin

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools

entries.name: Tutanota
entries.section: 🧰 The Workshop — Utilities & Swiss-Army Tools
